q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: WITH CTE AS (SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) CT FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID) SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CTE WHERE CT=(SELECT COUNT(PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)

counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 checks if the number of distinct products a customer has purchased is equal to the total number of distinct products in the database. Q2 checks if the number of distinct products a customer has purchased is equal to the total number of products in the database, without considering distinctness.
counterexample_dsp: A customer has purchased all products, and there is only one product in the database.
